nodes.label: Kinematics
nodes.note: Rectilinear motion, projectile motion, and relative motion. JEE tests calculus-based kinematics, graph interpretation, and vector decomposition.

nodes.label: Rectilinear Motion Fundamentals
nodes.note: One-dimensional motion along a straight line: distance, displacement, velocity, and acceleration.

nodes.label: Distance vs Displacement
nodes.note: Distance is the total path length (scalar); displacement is the straight-line vector from initial to final position. The fundamental inequality is $$s \ge |\Delta \vec{r}|$$, with equality only for straight unidirectional motion.

nodes.label: Equality Condition
nodes.note: Distance equals displacement magnitude if and only if the particle moves along a strictly straight line without ever reversing direction.

nodes.label: Speed and Velocity
nodes.note: Average velocity is displacement over time; average speed is total distance over time. Always $$v_{\text{avg, scalar}} \ge |\vec{v}_{\text{avg}}|$$.

nodes.label: Average Velocity
nodes.note: $$\vec{v}_{\text{avg}} = \frac{\Delta \vec{r}}{\Delta t} = \frac{\vec{r}_f - \vec{r}_i}{t_f - t_i}$$. Instantaneous velocity is the limit as $$\Delta t \to 0$$: $$\vec{v} = \frac{d\vec{r}}{dt}$$.

nodes.label: Mean Speed Theorems
nodes.note: For equal distance segments, $$v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{2 v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}$$ (harmonic mean). For equal time intervals, $$v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{v_1 + v_2}{2}$$ (arithmetic mean).

nodes.label: Acceleration and Calculus
nodes.note: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity: $$\vec{a} = \frac{d\vec{v}}{dt} = \frac{d^2\vec{r}}{dt^2}$$. In one dimension, $$a = \frac{dv}{dt} = v\frac{dv}{dx}$$ by the chain rule.

nodes.label: Differential Form
nodes.note: The spatial form $$a = v \frac{dv}{dx}$$ is derived from $$\frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{dv}{dx}\frac{dx}{dt}$$. It is essential for position-dependent acceleration problems.

nodes.label: Uniformly Accelerated Motion
nodes.note: Motion with constant acceleration: the master equations, vertical free fall, and graph calculus.

nodes.label: Equations of Motion
nodes.note: The three master equations for constant acceleration: $$v = u + at$$, $$s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2 = \frac{u+v}{2}t$$, and $$v^2 = u^2 + 2as$$.

nodes.label: Displacement in nth Second
nodes.note: The displacement in the $$n$$-th second is $$s_n = u + \frac{a}{2}(2n-1)$$. This is not the total distance in $$n$$ seconds.

nodes.label: Vertical Motion Under Gravity
nodes.note: Taking upward as positive, a body projected up with speed $$u$$ decelerates at $$g$$. Time of ascent equals time of descent: $$t_a = t_d = \frac{u}{g}$$.

nodes.label: Maximum Height
nodes.note: At maximum height $$v = 0$$, so $$H_{\max} = \frac{u^2}{2g}$$. The body returns to projection level with the same speed $$u$$.

nodes.label: Dual Time Conjugates
nodes.note: For any height $$h < H_{\max}$$, the two times $$t_1$$ (ascending) and $$t_2$$ (descending) satisfy $$t_1 + t_2 = \frac{2u}{g}$$ and $$t_1 t_2 = \frac{2h}{g}$$.

nodes.label: Kinematics Graphs
nodes.note: The slope of an $$x$$-t graph gives velocity; the slope of a $$v$$-t graph gives acceleration. The area under a $$v$$-t graph gives signed displacement.

nodes.label: Area Under v-t Graph
nodes.note: The algebraic area under a $$v$$-t curve yields displacement ($$\Delta x = \int v\,dt$$). For total distance, take the absolute value: $$s = \int |v|\,dt$$.

nodes.label: Area Under a-x Graph
nodes.note: The area under an acceleration-displacement curve gives $$\int a\,dx = \frac{v_f^2 - v_i^2}{2}$$. This is the work-energy relation per unit mass.

nodes.label: Galileo's Law of Odd Numbers
nodes.note: For a particle starting from rest under uniform acceleration, displacements in consecutive equal time intervals follow the ratio $$s_1 : s_2 : s_3 : \dots = 1 : 3 : 5 : \dots : (2n-1)$$.

nodes.label: Stopping Distance
nodes.note: Total stopping distance combines reaction distance and braking distance: $$D_{\text{stop}} = u t_r + \frac{u^2}{2a}$$. Reaction distance scales linearly with speed; braking distance scales quadratically.

nodes.label: Projectile Motion
nodes.note: Two-dimensional motion under uniform gravity: independence of horizontal and vertical components, flight parameters, and trajectory geometry.

nodes.label: Independence of Motion
nodes.note: A projectile's horizontal motion is uniform ($$v_x = u\cos\theta = \text{const}$$) and vertical motion is uniformly accelerated ($$a_y = -g$$). The two components are completely independent.

nodes.label: Flight Parameters
nodes.note: Time of flight, maximum height, and range are the three canonical flight parameters for ground-to-ground projectiles.

nodes.label: Time of Flight
nodes.note: Setting $$y = 0$$ gives $$T = \frac{2u\sin\theta}{g}$$. Time of ascent equals time of descent: $$t_a = t_d = \frac{T}{2}$$.

nodes.label: Height and Range
nodes.note: Maximum height is $$H_{\max} = \frac{u^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}$$ and horizontal range is $$R = \frac{u^2\sin 2\theta}{g}$$. The geometric link is $$\tan\theta = \frac{4H_{\max}}{R}$$.

nodes.label: Maximum Range
nodes.note: For fixed $$u$$, range is maximized at $$\theta = 45^\circ$$ giving $$R_{\max} = \frac{u^2}{g}$$. The height at maximum range is $$H = \frac{u^2}{4g}$$.

nodes.label: Equation of Trajectory
nodes.note: Eliminating time from the kinematic equations yields the parabolic trajectory $$y = x\tan\theta - \frac{gx^2}{2u^2\cos^2\theta}$$.

nodes.label: Factorized Range Form
nodes.note: The trajectory can be rewritten as $$y = x\tan\theta\left(1 - \frac{x}{R}\right)$$. This form is ideal for clearance problems over walls and obstacles.

nodes.label: Complementary Angles
nodes.note: Two projectiles launched at the same speed $$u$$ at angles $$\theta$$ and $$90^\circ - \theta$$ have identical ranges: $$R(\theta) = R(90^\circ - \theta)$$.

nodes.label: Inter-Trajectory Relations
nodes.note: For complementary angles, $$T_1 T_2 = \frac{2R}{g}$$ and $$R = 4\sqrt{H_1 H_2}$$. Also $$H_1 + H_2 = \frac{u^2}{2g}$$ and $$\frac{T_1}{T_2} = \tan\theta$$.

nodes.label: Radius of Curvature
nodes.note: The radius of curvature at any point on the trajectory is $$\rho = \frac{v^2}{a_\perp}$$ where $$a_\perp$$ is the normal component of acceleration.

nodes.label: Curvature at Peak
nodes.note: At the topmost point, $$v = u\cos\theta$$ and $$a_\perp = g$$, so $$\rho_{\text{top}} = \frac{u^2\cos^2\theta}{g}$$. This is the global minimum radius of curvature.

nodes.label: Inclined Plane Ballistics
nodes.note: On an incline of angle $$\beta$$, choose axes along and perpendicular to the incline. The launch angle $$\alpha$$ is measured relative to the incline surface.

nodes.label: Optimal Launch Angles
nodes.note: Maximum range up the incline occurs at $$\alpha = 45^\circ - \frac{\beta}{2}$$ giving $$R_{\text{up,max}} = \frac{u^2}{g(1+\sin\beta)}$$. Down the incline, $$\alpha = 45^\circ + \frac{\beta}{2}$$ gives $$R_{\text{down,max}} = \frac{u^2}{g(1-\sin\beta)}$$.

nodes.label: Relative Motion
nodes.note: Frame transformations, closest approach geometry, and classic 2D relative motion problems.

nodes.label: Frame Transformations
nodes.note: Relative position, velocity, and acceleration follow vector subtraction: $$\vec{r}_{B/A} = \vec{r}_B - \vec{r}_A$$, $$\vec{v}_{B/A} = \vec{v}_B - \vec{v}_A$$, $$\vec{a}_{B/A} = \vec{a}_B - \vec{a}_A$$.

nodes.label: Two-Projectile Theorem
nodes.note: Two projectiles in flight under gravity have $$\vec{a}_{\text{rel}} = \vec{g} - \vec{g} = 0$$. Their relative motion is uniform straight-line at constant velocity $$\vec{v}_{2/1} = \vec{u}_2 - \vec{u}_1$$.

nodes.label: Closest Approach
nodes.note: The velocity of approach is $$v_{\text{app}} = -\frac{dr}{dt}$$. At closest approach, $$v_{\text{app}} = 0$$ and the relative velocity is perpendicular to the line of sight.

nodes.label: Closest Approach Geometry
nodes.note: For initial separation $$r_0$$ and relative velocity at angle $$\theta$$ to the line of sight, $$d_{\min} = r_0\sin\theta$$ and $$t_{\min} = \frac{r_0\cos\theta}{|\vec{v}_{\text{rel}}|}$$.

nodes.label: River-Boat Crossing
nodes.note: A boat crosses a river of width $$d$$ with current speed $$v_r$$ and boat speed $$u$$ relative to water. Shortest time and shortest path are different strategies.

nodes.label: Shortest Time
nodes.note: Steer perpendicular to the bank ($$\theta = 90^\circ$$): $$t_{\min} = \frac{d}{u}$$. The downstream drift is $$x = \frac{v_r d}{u}$$. Crossing time is independent of river speed.

nodes.label: Zero Drift
nodes.note: To land directly opposite, steer upstream with $$\sin\alpha = \frac{v_r}{u}$$ (requires $$u > v_r$$). The crossing time is $$t = \frac{d}{\sqrt{u^2 - v_r^2}}$$.

nodes.label: Minimum Drift When Slower
nodes.note: When $$u < v_r$$, zero drift is impossible. The minimum drift is $$x_{\min} = d\sqrt{\frac{v_r^2}{u^2} - 1}$$ achieved at $$\sin\alpha = \frac{u}{v_r}$$.

nodes.label: Rain-Man Problem
nodes.note: Rain falls with velocity $$\vec{v}_r$$ and a person moves with velocity $$\vec{v}_m$$. The apparent rain velocity is $$\vec{v}_{r/m} = \vec{v}_r - \vec{v}_m$$.

nodes.label: Umbrella Tilt
nodes.note: To stay dry, hold the umbrella opposite to the apparent rain direction. The tilt angle from vertical is $$\tan\theta = \frac{|v_{rx} + v_m|}{v_{ry}}$$. For vertical rain, $$\tan\theta = \frac{v_m}{v_r}$$.

nodes.label: Polygon Pursuit
nodes.note: $$N$$ particles at the vertices of a regular $$N$$-gon each move toward their cyclic neighbor at speed $$v$$. They spiral into the center.

nodes.label: Pursuit Time
nodes.note: The approach speed is $$v_{\text{app}} = v[1 - \cos(2\pi/N)]$$, so the meeting time is $$t_{\text{meet}} = \frac{d}{v[1 - \cos(2\pi/N)]}$$. For a triangle, $$t = \frac{2d}{3v}$$; for a square, $$t = \frac{d}{v}$$.
